## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### Through an API

api (Alibaba Cloud Model Studio) · $0.60/M blended · $0.3 in / $1.5 out per 1M tokens · [alibabacloud.com](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing)

<sub>[price source](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing): USD per 1M tokens, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, Singapore (International deployment scope), qwen3-coder-next, lowest input tier (0 \< input tokens per request ≤ 32K). Requests with 32K–128K input are billed $0.5/$2.5 and 128K–256K $0.8/$4. Free quota and context-cache discounts excluded. Currency: USD. Alibaba Cloud official Model Studio pricing page, observed 2026-09-25. · [context source](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/blob/a668908cfe7073faa0363699486fc41a3ff52412/models/alibaba/qwen3-coder-next.toml): model catalogue context ceiling (not a promise by a hosted API)</sub>

### llama.cpp (recommended)

1. Install llama.cpp. Homebrew and winget installs name the commands llama-cli and llama-server instead. [Other ways to install](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md)
   
   ```sh
   # macOS / Linux
   curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh
   # Windows
   irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex
   ```

2. Run Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B) (ud-q2_k_xl, needs ~24.41 GB, from [huggingface.co/unsloth](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF/tree/main))
   
   ```sh
   llama cli -hf unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL
   ```

3. Or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
   
   ```sh
   llama serve -hf unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL
   ```

### LM Studio

1. Install LM Studio. Open the app once before using the lms command. [Download it (macOS / Windows / Linux)](https://lmstudio.ai/download)

2. Run Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B) (4bit, needs ~44.8 GB, Mac only, from [huggingface.co/lmstudio-community](https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit/tree/03cba26036330b7553d252c1f3fb899f16cc5ea5))
   
   ```sh
   lms get https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit -y
   ```

3. Then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name

Other versions: ud-q2_k_xl (~24.41 GB) `lms get https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF@UD-Q2_K_XL -y` · 8bit (~84.7 GB, Mac only) `lms get https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-8bit -y`

### Ollama

1. Install Ollama. [Download it (macOS / Windows)](https://ollama.com/download)
   
   ```sh
   # Linux
   curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
   ```

2. Run Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B) (Q4_K_M, needs ~48.32 GB, from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/library/qwen3-coder-next/tags))
   
   ```sh
   ollama run qwen3-coder-next
   ```

### MLX (Mac)

1. Install MLX (Mac). Apple silicon Macs only, text only.
   
   ```sh
   # with uv
   uv tool install mlx-lm
   # or
   pip install mlx-lm
   ```

2. Run Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B) (4bit, needs ~44.8 GB, Mac only, from [huggingface.co/lmstudio-community](https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit/tree/03cba26036330b7553d252c1f3fb899f16cc5ea5))
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.chat --model lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit
   ```

3. Or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.server --model lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit
   ```

Other versions: 8bit (~84.7 GB, Mac only) `mlx_lm.chat --model lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-8bit`

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/Qwen](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next)
